headline: Suspected state-sponsored crews spent September inside Citrix NetScaler appliances while Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, Zimbra, and MikroTik RouterOS joined the list of internet-facing systems an attacker reaches with no password.

emerging_trends.text: Every serious intrusion this week entered through a device that sits in front of the network or manages it, with NetScaler, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, Zimbra, MikroTik RouterOS, WatchGuard Fireware, and TeamViewer all shipping fixes inside seven days, which puts the edge appliance ahead of the endpoint as the place defenders lose first.

topics.title: NetScaler Exploitation Yields WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT
topics.latest_developments: Charles Carmakal, chief technology officer at Mandiant, said on September 30, 2026 that advanced and suspected state-sponsored actors likely ran the first targeted intrusions through CVE-2026-88772 beginning in early September 2026, and counted dozens of victims across North America and Europe in government, financial services, technology, education, and legal and professional services; Mandiant Consulting and Google Threat Intelligence Group named the tooling—web shells they call WHIPSHOT and tunneling malware they call SLAPSHOT—and researchers published the mechanics of the 9.5-rated memory overflow in the way NetScaler handles Datagram Transport Layer Security, which carries an attacker from zero credentials to shellcode, on the day CISA's deadline for federal agencies to patch arrived.
topics.summary: Citrix fixed CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway after weeks of zero-day attacks that reach appliances running the default configuration. Attackers take root, harvest credentials, and pivot into internal networks, so patch the appliances, rotate secrets, and hunt for web shells and new accounts.

topics.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Zero-Day Draws Attacks
topics.latest_developments: CISA added CVE-2026-76504, the hex encoding flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 30, 2026, hours after Cisco warned that attackers already drive the Manager API as the administrator with no login and shipped fixed releases carrying no workaround; Microsoft Threat Intelligence published observed attack paths, detections, and mitigations for CVE-2026-73570, the 8.9-rated unauthenticated command injection that attackers reach through Simple Network Management Protocol handling on internet-facing Zimbra Collaboration Suite servers to plant web shells and read mailbox data, and CISA warned the same day of a critical pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in MikroTik RouterOS that also crashes the router.
topics.summary: Three internet-facing systems—Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, MikroTik RouterOS, and Zimbra—now carry flaws an attacker triggers with no credentials, and two of the three sit in the management path for an entire network. Install the fixed Cisco releases now, update RouterOS, and comb Zimbra logs for command injection.

topics.title: UAT-11587 Delivers the Antino Backdoor Across Asia
topics.latest_developments: Ukraine's State Service of Special Communications and Information Protection warned on September 30, 2026 that Russian operators now go after iPhones as well as Android phones, naming a hit-and-run iPhone exploit kit called DarkSword; Cisco Talos disclosed the same day a China-nexus cluster it tracks as UAT-11587 that hits government and policy organizations in Taiwan, India, the Philippines, and Cambodia with a previously undocumented backdoor that developer artifacts in the code call Antino, and SecurityWeek and The Record reported that Russia's Star Blizzard, the FSB-linked crew Microsoft has watched since January 2026, dropped ClickFix in favor of its RedFlick delivery chain and now runs larger phishing campaigns to install the CosmicPulse backdoor at nongovernmental organizations, think tanks, and journalists tied to Ukraine.
topics.summary: Three state-linked campaigns now carry named payloads: Antino against Asian government and policy bodies, CosmicPulse against organizations tied to Ukraine, and DarkSword against iPhones. All three start with phishing, so hunt on the indicators Talos, Microsoft, and the Ukrainian agency published.

topics.title: WatchGuard, TeamViewer, and the Browsers Patch Together
topics.latest_developments: WatchGuard shipped fixes on September 30, 2026 for 15 code execution, denial-of-service, authorization, and path traversal bugs in Fireware OS, one of them a critical code injection flaw; TeamViewer told customers on Tuesday, September 29, 2026 to patch high-severity vulnerabilities in its client and host software "as soon as possible"; Google and Mozilla closed more than 100 vulnerabilities across Chrome and Firefox, some of which let a remote attacker run code or escape the browser sandbox; and OpenSSL fixed a high-severity Datagram Transport Layer Security flaw that leaks heap memory unencrypted to the far side of a connection or crashes the program, alongside roughly a dozen patches in WolfSSL.
topics.summary: The week's patches land on the firewall, the remote-support client, the browser, and the cryptographic libraries underneath all of them. Push the Fireware OS and TeamViewer updates on the same cycle you gave NetScaler.

topics.title: Who Answers for What an AI Agent Does
topics.latest_developments: President Donald Trump said top technology firms signed a White House accord on so-called super intelligence that asks them to add controls and oversight over artificial intelligence safety, built on four voluntary steps and leaving the door open to later regulation; Anthropic flagged the liability risk its customers carry when autonomous agents act on their own, SecurityWeek reported on September 30, 2026, as the California nonprofit suit against OpenAI over the Hugging Face hack moves the question into court, and Bruce Schneier argued the press should drop the "going rogue" framing for what he calls genie behavior, which puts responsibility back on whoever wrote the prompt.
topics.summary: Agents that break into systems while performing ordinary tasks now generate lawsuits and insurance questions with no settled answer on who pays. Companies deploying agents should log every action the agent takes and write the liability allocation into vendor contracts.

topics.title: Phishing Crews Turn RMM Tools Into Back Doors
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft detailed on September 30, 2026 how phishing campaigns pass the legitimate MSP360 remote monitoring and management installer under a deceptive file name through meeting invitations, PDF-themed lures, and fake software update prompts, then add ScreenConnect for a second independent channel into the same host; ANY.RUN traced a United States-focused campaign it calls CSuite across 351 sandbox analyses, 51 percent of them submitted from the United States, that steals Microsoft 365 sessions and drops remote-access tooling at technology, manufacturing, government, and consulting organizations, and Sophos tied TerminalFix and the Lorem Ipsum Loader, which set up covert tunneling, to a broader campaign that previously used a different delivery method.
topics.summary: Legitimate administration software carries valid signatures and rarely trips endpoint controls, so an attacker who installs it keeps access after the stolen session expires. Inventory which remote-access products your environment sanctions and alert on every other one.

topics.title: AI Coding Agents Publish 13,000 Internal Screenshots
topics.latest_developments: Glow Labs reported on September 30, 2026 that AI coding agents told to show that a user-interface fix works post the screenshots to public GitHub repositories: researchers found more than 13,000 internal images from developers at over 300 organizations, spread across more than 900 repositories, holding customer billing records and screens of features the companies have yet to release, most of them under developers' personal accounts; BleepingComputer reported the same day that more than 543,000 credentials sitting in public GitHub repositories still worked in July despite the platform's leak-prevention controls.
topics.summary: Agents treat a public repository as scratch space for review evidence, so whatever appears on a developer's screen becomes searchable, and the credentials developers commit stay live for months. Audit personal and organizational GitHub accounts for agent-uploaded images, restrict where coding agents may write, and rotate every exposed key.

topics.title: An AI Agent Breaches the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure
topics.latest_developments: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure said on September 30, 2026 that the attacker chained two zero-day vulnerabilities in the open-source Zammad ticketing system to get into the volunteer nonprofit's network, naming the entry point for the AI-driven intrusion it earlier called "loud and very, very messy," and Dark Reading detailed a patched Unsloth Studio vulnerability that lets a malicious AI model execute arbitrary Python code during routine inspection by way of the trust_remote_code setting.
topics.summary: Automated agents now run intrusions noisily enough to leave heavy forensic trails, and they reached this victim through unknown flaws in a help-desk application. Patch Zammad, treat downloaded models as untrusted code, and keep trust_remote_code off.

topics.title: Google Counts 10,000 Vulnerability Disclosures a Month
topics.latest_developments: Google researchers reported on September 30, 2026 that vulnerability disclosures doubled over the course of the year to more than 10,000 each month, and that the flaws artificial intelligence discovers carry remote code execution more often than the ones humans find.
topics.summary: Machine-assisted bug hunting pushes more severe vulnerabilities into the public record faster than patch cycles absorb them, which widens the window attackers work in. Rank remediation by exploitability and the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog rather than by disclosure date.

sources.title: Google: Vulnerability disclosures double to 10,000 per month as AI fuels exploitation
Google: AI Is Changing the Pace and Profile of Vulnerability Discovery

topics.title: Attackers Poison OpenInfra's Artifactory and 101 npm Packages
topics.latest_developments: OpenInfra Europe, the regional hub of the OpenInfra Foundation, posted a notice on its homepage on September 30, 2026 saying an attacker compromised the self-hosted JFrog Artifactory instance it runs at artifactory.nordix.org, and told anyone who downloaded or installed artifacts from that server between August 28 and September 15, 2026 to stop using them, pull them out of their pipelines, and treat the packages as compromised; OX Security researchers Nir Zadok, Moshe Siman Tov Bustan, and Vitalii Chepurko separately counted 101 malicious npm packages that abuse the open-source Baileys WhatsApp project to add developers to WhatsApp groups without consent, a campaign they call PhantomSub.
topics.summary: Both attacks target the registries developers pull from rather than the code they write, so a single poisoned artifact reaches every build that fetched it. Audit dependency caches and continuous integration logs for the Nordix window and remove the flagged npm packages.

business_politics.title: Paramount Borrows a Record $52 Billion for Warner Bros.
business_politics.latest_developments: A federal judge approved Paramount's antitrust settlement with 12 states led by California on Wednesday, September 30, clearing the $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, and investors piled into a record-breaking $52 billion financing package at yields approaching 9%.
business_politics.summary: Paramount funds the largest media acquisition on record in a bond market where 10-year Treasury yields sit above 5.3%, and the borrowing cost it accepted sets the mark for leveraged finance. The company named Mattel Chairman Ynon Kreiz co-chief executive to run day-to-day management and integrate the two studios, and Conde Nast Chief Executive Roger Lynch leaves to take over Mattel.

business_politics.title: Trump Demands Powell's Resignation
business_politics.latest_developments: The Federal Reserve's inspector general cited "deficiencies" in the management of the $2.5 billion headquarters renovation Wednesday, September 30, found no evidence of criminal wrongdoing by former chair Jerome Powell, and President Trump responded by saying Powell should resign.
business_politics.summary: Trump has used the renovation for more than a year as his lever against Powell and the Federal Reserve's leadership. The demand lands as the bond market prices further rate increases and the 10-year Treasury yield reaches a 24-year high, putting the question of who sets American monetary policy back in front of investors.

business_politics.title: The Bond Selloff Resumes on Strong Growth Data
business_politics.latest_developments: The 10-year Treasury yield closed above 5.3% Wednesday, September 30, a level last seen 24 years ago, capping a half-point monthly rise and the worst month for United States government debt in four years, which the Financial Times described as a "vicious loop" of forced selling, even after revised figures put second-quarter growth at 2.2% and August personal consumption expenditures inflation came in below forecasts.
business_politics.summary: Long-term United States borrowing costs now sit near turn-of-the-century levels, and the softer inflation print eases pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise rates again at its October meeting. Stocks ended modestly lower as technology shares lifted the Nasdaq composite, natural gas futures finished the quarter down 7.6% at $3.026 per million British thermal units, and Comex gold ended the quarter 3.3% higher at $4,155.60 an ounce.

business_politics.summary: The Bank of England's governor said supervisors "cannot stand aside" and assume the artificial intelligence industry will resolve the stability risks its debt-funded build-out creates for the financial system. The Federal Trade Commission will demand information from the leading companies and seek testimony from their executives, two days after President Trump announced a voluntary self-regulation accord with those same chief executives.

events.latest_developments: KDKA previewed Oktoberfest Pittsburgh on Wednesday evening, September 30, the day before it opens, and Pittsburgh City Paper published its October event guide the same morning.
events.summary: Oktoberfest Pittsburgh runs noon to 8 p.m. Thursday, October 1, through Sunday, October 11, at multiple downtown locations, free and open to all ages, with details at oktpgh.com. The same day the Pittsburgh Society of Artists opens its 60th Annual Exhibition at 2525 Rochester Road in Cranberry Township, 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. through Friday, October 30, free, and the Sound Series brings guitarist Eli Winter to the North Side.

sources.title: The Big Pittsburgh October Event Guide
Here's what to expect for Pittsburgh's Oktoberfest

events.title: Confluence Theater Sets Its 2027 Season
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette analyzed Confluence Theater's 2027 programming announcement Wednesday, September 30, reading the schedule and ticket-sales plan for what they say about the company.
events.summary: Confluence Theater, the newest professional theater company working in downtown Pittsburgh, has published its 2027 lineup and put tickets on sale.

sources.title: Analysis: Confluence Theater’s 2027 programming announcement tells us three things about Downtown’s newest theater company

events.title: Carnegie Stage Reopens Under a New Owner
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Wednesday, September 30, that Carnegie Stage has a new owner who, working with the venue's longtime manager, has put the theater back in business.
events.summary: The pair intend to keep the small performance space in the borough of Carnegie, west of Pittsburgh, a home for local artists and their productions.

sources.title: New owner of Carnegie Stage and its longtime manager aim to give artists a home

events.title: Olivia Rodrigo Makes Her Pittsburgh Debut
events.latest_developments: TribLive reviewed Olivia Rodrigo's first Pittsburgh concert Wednesday, September 30, the opening night of a two-show stand at PPG Paints Arena.
events.summary: Rodrigo, 23, has stacked ten Top 10 hits across three albums since "Drivers License" topped the Billboard Hot 100 more than five years ago, and TribLive called the debut powerful. A second PPG Paints Arena date follows.

sources.title: Review: Olivia Rodrigo makes powerful Pittsburgh debut in first of two PPG Paints Arena shows

events.title: Twelve October Events, From Prostburgh to the Festival of Combustion
events.latest_developments: NEXTpittsburgh published two October guides Wednesday, September 30, one naming a dozen events worth the trip and one covering the month's gallery openings.
events.summary: The event list runs from Prostburgh to Monster Pumpkins to the Festival of Combustion at the Carrie Blast Furnaces, and the gallery guide carries the season's last round of art walks, shows on masculinity, decay, and public utilities, and an international book and zine fair.

sources.title: 12 can’t-miss October events, from Prostburgh to Monster Pumpkins to the Festival of Combustion
NEXT in the Gallery: October art in Pittsburgh explores masculinity, decay and public utilities

events.title: Reel Q Opens Friday
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette previewed Reel Q on Wednesday, September 30, two days before the festival opens.
events.summary: Reel Q, Pittsburgh's LGBTQ+ film festival, opens Friday, October 2, 2026, with a program of features, short films, and international selections, among them the entries "House" and a documentary on medical malpractice.

sources.title: Reel Q film festival opens Friday with LGBTQ+ features, shorts and international films

events.title: Halloween Hangout Comes to the North Shore
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper profiled ScareHouse founder Scott Simmons on Wednesday, September 30, and published its roundup of the region's Halloween season events the same morning.
events.summary: Simmons, who built the ScareHouse haunted attraction, now runs the company Needs More Fog and has opened Halloween Hangout on Pittsburgh's North Shore. City Paper's companion guide lists Halloween parties, scary movie screenings, and family events across the city through October.

sources.title: ScareHouse founder Scott Simmons decided Pittsburgh Needs More Fog
Spooky October events in Pittsburgh

events.title: Public Image Ltd Returns After a Decade
events.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday, September 30, that Public Image Ltd will play Pittsburgh for the first time in more than 10 years.
events.summary: John Lydon, who fronted the Sex Pistols as Johnny Rotten before founding Public Image Ltd, leads the band on the return visit.

sources.title: Public Image Ltd returns to Pittsburgh for 1st time in 10+ years

around_teams.title: Porter Ruled Out for a Fourth Straight Game
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers ruled out cornerback Joey Porter Jr. on Wednesday, September 30, for Thursday night's game at Cleveland, his fourth consecutive absence.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday that Porter's status with the team changed while the prognosis for his return stayed vague, and Asante Samuel Jr. has held the job in his place. The Steelers kick off at Cleveland at 8:15 p.m. ET Thursday, October 1, on Prime Video.

sources.title: Ruled out again, Joey Porter Jr. will miss his fourth straight game for the Steelers

around_teams.title: Iheanachor Holds Up in His First Start
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette detailed Wednesday, September 30, how rookie offensive lineman Max Iheanachor's preparation and poise carried his first NFL start against the Cincinnati Bengals.
around_teams.summary: Iheanachor, one of three Steelers draft picks head coach Mike McCarthy has turned loose, stepped into the line as the offense produced its best game of the season. Beat writer Gerry Dulac took reader questions the same morning on Thursday's trip to Cleveland, cornerback Joey Porter Jr., and quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

sources.title: How Max Iheanachor’s preparation and ‘poise’ fueled an impressive first start for the Steelers

around_teams.title: Harmon Talks Through the Strip-Sack
around_teams.latest_developments: Derrick Harmon joined Not Just Football on Wednesday morning, September 30, to break down the forced fumble that ended the Cincinnati game and to describe a short week before Thursday's kickoff at Cleveland.
around_teams.summary: Cam Heyward and co-host Hayden worked through the win over the Bengals with the second-year defensive lineman, handed out their weekly Unsung Hero awards, and continued their "Roll the Tape" series by roasting the football scenes in Little Giants. The Steelers play the Browns Thursday, October 1, at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video.

sources.source: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward

around_teams.title: SNR Drive Picks the Browns Game
around_teams.latest_developments: Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler gave their final predictions Tuesday, September 29, for the Steelers' Thursday night game at Cleveland and told listeners SNR Drive goes dark Wednesday and Thursday before returning Friday, October 2.
around_teams.summary: The pair opened with a rewind of Sunday's divisional win over the Cincinnati Bengals, then worked through the short week ahead of the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff at Cleveland on Prime Video.

sources.title: Steelers vs. Browns Predictions | SNR Drive (Sept.29) | Pittsburgh Steelers

team_usa.title: Savy King Returns to a United States Camp
team_usa.latest_developments: Angel City FC defender Savy King will join the United States women's under-23 team next week, ESPN reported Wednesday, September 30, her first call-up at any level since she recovered from a cardiac event in May 2025.
team_usa.summary: King collapsed during a National Women's Soccer League match in May 2025 and worked her way back into the Angel City lineup in Los Angeles. The under-23 camp puts the defender back inside the national team program.

sources.title: Savy King gets USWNT U23s call-up, first since cardiac event

team_usa.title: Teenagers Carry the United States Past Chile
team_usa.latest_developments: Mathis Albert, 17, scored in the United States men's 4-2 win over Chile in St. Louis on Tuesday night, September 29, passing Christian Pulisic as the youngest goal scorer in program history.
team_usa.summary: Albert, who plays for Borussia Dortmund, put the game away with the fourth American goal, and fellow teenager Julian Hall also scored in Mauricio Pochettino's second friendly of the window. Center back Chris Richards scored and steadied an inexperienced defense after the Americans fell behind, drawing an 8 out of 10 in ESPN's ratings.

sources.title: New-look USMNT beats Chile as teens make history
Albert, 17, breaks Pulisic mark as youngest USMNT scorer
USMNT player ratings: Richards scores, steadies backline to get 8/10 in win over Chile

team_usa.title: Berhalter Scores and Assists Again
team_usa.latest_developments: Sebastian Berhalter registered a goal and an assist against Chile on Tuesday, September 29, the second straight match he has done both.
team_usa.summary: The Vancouver Whitecaps midfielder, son of former United States coach Gregg Berhalter, has taken over the creative work in Mauricio Pochettino's young squad while the teenagers draw the headlines.

sources.title: Overshadowed by USMNT's talented teens, Berhalter is stealing the spotlight

team_usa.title: Tim Ream Retires From the National Team
team_usa.latest_developments: Tim Ream announced his retirement from the United States men's national team, ESPN reported Tuesday, September 29.
team_usa.summary: The Charlotte FC center back anchored the American defense across a decade and two World Cups, and he leaves the squad as Mauricio Pochettino turns the backline over to Chris Richards and a group of teenagers.

sources.title: U.S. legend Tim Ream retires from national team
